facts.evidence: **Net Income Applicable to Morgan Stanley:** $5.6 billion (up 58% from $3.5 billion in 2025) ... **Earnings Per Diluted Share:** $3.46 (up 62% from $2.13 in 2025)
**Net Revenues:** $11.0 billion (up 45% from $7.6 billion in 2025) ... **Record Revenues Driven by Equity and Investment Banking**
**Return on Tangible Common Equity (ROTCE):** 26.6% (up from 18.2% in 2025)
**Record Net New Assets:** $148 billion, with $74 billion from IPOs in the Workplace channel

claims.claim: Second quarter 2026 net revenues were $21.3 billion.
Net revenues were up 27% from $16.8 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was up 58% from $3.5 billion in 2025.
Earnings per diluted share were $3.46.
Earnings per diluted share were up 62% from $2.13 in 2025.
Return on tangible common equity was 26.6%.
ROTCE was up from 18.2% in 2025.
Institutional Securities net revenues were $11.0 billion, compared with $7.6 billion in 2025.
Institutional Securities net revenues were up 45% year over year.
claims.note: The release gives no percentage change for Institutional Securities net revenues; $11,040M vs $7,643M is +44%, so the figure is both uncalculated in the release and incorrectly rounded.

claims.claim: Institutional Securities revenues were a record.
The record Institutional Securities revenues were driven by Equity and Investment Banking.
Institutional Securities Equity net revenues were up 69%.
Institutional Securities Investment Banking net revenues were up 58%.
Wealth Management net revenues were $8.9 billion.
Wealth Management net revenues were up 14% from $7.8 billion in 2025.
Wealth Management net new assets of $148 billion were a record.
$74 billion of Wealth Management net new assets came from IPOs in the Workplace channel.
claims.note: The release says only that 'just over half' of the $148 billion related to IPOs of certain Workplace clients; the $74 billion figure is an unshown calculation and understates an amount the release describes as more than half.

claims.claim: Investment Management net revenues were $1.6 billion.
Investment Management net revenues were up 6% from $1.5 billion in 2025.
Investment Management asset management fees increased, driven by higher average AUM and positive flows.
The release does not provide any outlook or guidance for future periods.
The Standardized CET1 capital ratio was 14.8%.
Book value per share was $67.80.
Tangible book value per share was $53.18.
The expense efficiency ratio was 65%, down from 71% in 2025.
The expense efficiency ratio indicates improved operating leverage.
A significant portion of the $148 billion of Wealth Management net new assets came from IPOs.
Provision for credit losses was $98 million, down from $196 million in 2025.
The provision for credit losses reflected portfolio growth and individual assessments.
claims.note: The release attributes portfolio growth in corporate loans and secured lending facilities and individual assessments to the Institutional Securities provision ($71M), not to the Firm's $98M, and gives no driver for the year-over-year decline.
